land.text: Kizzuwatna, which 'rebelled during Suppiluliuma I's reign but stayed inside the Hittite Empire for roughly two centuries'

successors.note: Annexation year not on any page opened; the c. 1350 BC bridge is Suppiluliuma's accession on the Arzawa page. Quwe (Hiyawa) 'emerged in the former territory of Kizzuwatna' after the Empire fell (Kizzuwatna page); it belongs to the Neo-Hittite states. [Reviewer me-04-x, 2026-10-19: land changed from the whole Cliopatria Hittites -1400 shape, which by this dossier's own keyframe note has no Cilician cell, to the land actually handed over, the Cilicia region of the keyframe; the Kizzuwatna page: 'situated primarily in the Cilician Plain' and 'remained within the Hittite Empire for 200 years'.]

capitals.name: Kummanni
capitals.note: The page calls Kummanni 'the centre of the kingdom' in the highlands but gives no coordinates; the dot is a placeholder at Adana, the centre of the Cilician plain, until a gap-filler locates Kummanni.

correction.text: the Cilician Plain between the Taurus Mountains, the Amanus Range and the Mediterranean Sea

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Kizzuwatna. The page gives its limits as 'the Taurus Mountains, the Amanus Range, and the Mediterranean Sea' around the Cilician Plain; the gazetteer's Cilicia (Adana, Mersin, Osmaniye, about 30,000 km2) is the researcher's reading. The infobox gives no area, so nothing was compared with Cliopatria; Cliopatria's Hittite shapes of -1500 (57,838 km2, no Cilician cell south of 37.0 N) leave Cilicia out, and the -1400 shape (167,244 km2) adds it. Tudhaliya I's treaty (c. 1400 BC) freed Kizzuwatna from Mitanni but is described as a treaty between equals, so the -1400 Hittite shape is early for Cilicia by about fifty years.

region.text: the Cilician Plain between the Taurus Mountains, the Amanus Range and the Mediterranean Sea

ledger.note: c. 1500 BC: Kizzuwatna appears in the Cilician plain. The page gives no founding year; it is 'attested in written sources from the end of the 16th century BC onwards'. The Hittites page has Telepinu (c. 1500 BC) 'allying himself with one Hurrian state (Kizzuwatna) against another'; the Telipinu page (reign c. 1525 - c. 1500 BC) has the same alliance.

region.text: the Cilician Plain between the Taurus Mountains, the Amanus Range and the Mediterranean Sea

ledger.note: c. 1480 BC: Kizzuwatna is a Mitanni vassal. The Idrimi page has the tablet that 'dates back to c. 1480 BC. It was a treaty that Idrimi made with another vassal ruler to Mitanni, Pilliya of Kizzuwatna.' The start of the Mitanni overlordship is not dated on any page; 1480 is the first dated evidence of it.

region.text: the Cilician Plain between the Taurus Mountains, the Amanus Range and the Mediterranean Sea

ledger.note: c. 1400 BC: Tudhaliya I frees Kizzuwatna from Mitanni. 'He made a treaty with Sunassura and freed Kizzuwatna from Mitanni's control' (paraphrase of the page, which gives no year). The year is the Hittites page's date for Tudhaliya I ('Tudhaliya I (c. 1400 BC) again allied with Kizzuwatna, then vanquished the Hurrian states of Aleppo and Mitanni'); the Tudhaliya I page dates the reign c. 1465 - c. 1440 BC and notes Kuhrt's 1430-1400, and calls the treaty with Sunassura 'equal'.

region.text: the Cilician Plain between the Taurus Mountains, the Amanus Range and the Mediterranean Sea

ledger.note: c. 1350 BC (bridged): Kizzuwatna is absorbed by Hatti. The page says only that Kizzuwatna 'rebelled during Suppiluliuma I's reign but stayed inside the Hittite Empire for roughly two centuries' and gives no year; Suppiluliuma 'came to the throne around 1350 BC' on the Arzawa page.

region.text: the Cilician Plain between the Taurus Mountains, the Amanus Range and the Mediterranean Sea

ledger.note: c. 1350 BC (bridged): the kingdom of Kizzuwatna ends as a separate state in the Hittite Empire, which it supplied with troops at Kadesh (c. 1274 BC) and in which it stayed until the Sea Peoples' time (c. 1200 BC); Quwe (Hiyawa) later 'emerged in the former territory of Kizzuwatna'.

wars.name: Tudhaliya I's campaign against Aleppo and Mitanni

zones.text: the Cilician Plain between the Taurus Mountains, the Amanus Range and the Mediterranean Sea

wars.outcome: Hittite victory: Tudhaliya I 'again allied with Kizzuwatna, then vanquished the Hurrian states of Aleppo and Mitanni'; Kizzuwatna leaves Mitannian domination by treaty with Sunassura.
wars.note: The year is the Hittites page's 'c. 1400 BC'. The Tudhaliya I page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tudhaliya_I) dates the reign c. 1465 - c. 1440 BC, so the campaign may be sixty years earlier.

wars.name: Kizzuwatna's rebellion under Suppiluliuma I
wars.outcome: Kizzuwatna 'rebelled during Suppiluliuma I's reign but stayed inside the Hittite Empire for roughly two centuries'; annexed.
wars.note: No year on the page. The span is Suppiluliuma's accession c. 1350 BC (Arzawa page) to the year before Mursili II's accession in 1321 BC (Mursili II page). Zones left empty because the loss is carried by the ledger, not by a contested interval.

certainty.note: The only boundaries on the page are natural: the Taurus, the Amanus and the sea.

sources.title: Kizzuwatna
sources.note: Location and limits, Kummanni, attested from the end of the 16th century BC, Sunassura and Tudhaliya I, the rebellion under Suppiluliuma I, Kadesh troops, Quwe. Opened twice (second time for the History paragraphs). No infobox in the text received.

sources.title: Tudhaliya I
sources.note: Reign c. 1465 - c. 1440 BC (Kuhrt 1430-1400); the 'equal treaty' with Sunassura; thin on dates.

sources.title: Telipinu
sources.note: Infobox reign c. 1525 - c. 1500 BC; alliance with Kizzuwatna.

sources.title: Hittites
sources.note: Telepinu c. 1500 BC and Tudhaliya I c. 1400 BC allied with Kizzuwatna; silent on annexation.

sources.title: Idrimi
sources.note: Idrimi c. 1490-1465 BC; Pilliya of Kizzuwatna a Mitanni vassal, treaty tablet c. 1480 BC.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kizzuwatna. Dates are thin: no page opened gives a founding, a treaty or an annexation year. The 1500 start is the 'end of the 16th century BC' attestation; the 1480 Mitanni vassalage is the Idrimi tablet; the 1400 liberation is the Hittites page's date for Tudhaliya I (the Tudhaliya I page gives c. 1465-1440); the 1350 end is Suppiluliuma's accession. Conflict with the Hittites dossier (me-04-a): it draws the Cilician lands as Hittite from -1400 (a bridge, per its own note); this dossier keeps Kizzuwatna a separate treaty partner until about 1350, so the renderer should draw Cilicia as Kizzuwatna in -1400..-1351 and not as Hittite land. Isputahsu's treaty with Telipinu, Pilliya's parity treaty with Zidanta II and the Pilliya/Sunassura reigns are undated on all pages. The placeholder capital is at Adana. Quwe/Hiyawa (after the Hittite collapse) belongs to the Neo-Hittite states dossier; the page budget of five pages was spent.
